User: I met my colleague Mark at the cooking class last night, and we had a great time learning new recipes together.
Assistant: Sounds fun — glad you had a good time! Would you like me to send or draft a follow-up to Mark? I can also search your inbox for his contact if you prefer.

Here are three quick message options — tell me which one to send (or edit), and whether to send now or save as a draft. If you want me to send, either give Mark’s email or ask me to search for him (suggest a search phrase like “Mark cooking class” or “Mark [last name]”).

1) Short thank-you
- Subject: Great meeting you at the cooking class
- Body: Hi Mark — it was great meeting you at the cooking class last night. I had a lot of fun learning the new recipes together. Thanks for the company — would you like to swap notes or try another class soon? Best, [Your name]

2) Share recipes/photos + follow-up
- Subject: Recipes & photos from last night
- Body: Hi Mark — I had a great time at the cooking class last night. I’m attaching the recipe notes and a couple of photos I took. If you’re interested, would you like to try one of the recipes together next weekend? Cheers, [Your name]

3) Professional / networking tone
- Subject: Nice to meet you at the cooking class
- Body: Hi Mark — it was a pleasure meeting you at the cooking class last night. I enjoyed our conversation and the recipes. If you’re open to it, I’d love to connect over coffee sometime to chat more about [shared topic]. Best regards, [Your name]

Which option do you want, any edits, and should I send it now or save as a draft?

User: Please remember that I started a new hobby of painting and spent the weekend creating a beautiful landscape piece.
Assistant: Got it — I’ll remember that you’ve started painting as a new hobby and that you spent the weekend creating a beautiful landscape piece.

I can use this when helping you later (for personalized follow-ups, social posts, reminders, finding classes or supplies, drafting messages about your painting, etc.). Would you like to add any details now (medium, title, a photo you want to share), or want me to do something with this info (e.g., mention it in a message to Mark, set a reminder to paint, or draft a post)?

User: Please remember that I spent time with my friend Emily last night discussing our upcoming trip to Italy.
Assistant: Got it — I’ll remember that you spent time with your friend Emily last night discussing your upcoming trip to Italy.

How would you like me to use that memory? I can:
- Add trip details (dates, destinations, itinerary) if you want to store more.
- Search your inbox for Emily’s contact and draft or send a follow-up message.
- Set reminders (packing list, bookings, deadlines).
- Draft travel-related emails or help plan the itinerary.

Tell me if you want to add any specifics (trip dates, Emily’s email, places you’ll visit) or if you’d like me to take one of the actions above.

User: I enjoyed catching up with my old college friend, Rachel, over brunch at a cozy cafe downtown this morning.
Assistant: Sounds lovely — glad you had a nice catch-up. Would you like me to save this as a memory (so I can use it later), or take an action now (draft or send a follow-up to Rachel, or search your inbox for her contact)?

If you want a follow-up message, here are three quick options — tell me which one to send (or edit), and whether to send now or save as a draft. If you’d like me to send, either give Rachel’s email or ask me to search (suggested search phrase: "Rachel brunch cozy cafe downtown").

1) Short & friendly
- Subject: Great seeing you today
- Body: Hi Rachel — it was so nice catching up over brunch this morning. I loved hearing about [topic you discussed]. Let’s do it again soon! — [Your name]

2) Share photos / plan another meetup
- Subject: Brunch today — photos & next time?
- Body: Hi Rachel — I had a lovely time at brunch today. I’m attaching a couple of photos from the cafe — would you like to meet up again next weekend for coffee or a walk? — [Your name]

3) Nostalgic / longer
- Subject: Love catching up — remind me of college days!
- Body: Hi Rachel — brunch this morning was wonderful. It was so fun reminiscing about our college days and hearing about what you’ve been up to. Let’s plan something soon — maybe dinner next month? — [Your name]

Which option do you want, any edits, and should I save this memory now?

User: Please remember that I tried a new restaurant with my friends last Friday, and we had a blast exploring the menu together.
Assistant: Got it — I’ll remember that you tried a new restaurant with your friends last Friday and had a blast exploring the menu together.

Would you like to add any details to the memory now (restaurant name, dishes you liked, which friends were there, photos), or should I just save it as-is? I can also:
- Draft a thank-you/follow-up message to the friends
- Save photos or draft a short review for you
- Set a reminder to book the restaurant again
- Search your inbox for related messages or reservations

What would you like me to do?

User: I caught up with my cousin Sarah yesterday over a virtual coffee date, and we shared updates on our families.
Assistant: Got it — I’ll remember that you caught up with your cousin Sarah yesterday over a virtual coffee date and shared updates on your families.

Would you like me to save any extra details now (Sarah’s email, children’s names/ages, time zone, topics you discussed), or do one of these actions?

- Search your inbox for Sarah’s contact and draft or send a follow-up
- Draft a quick thank-you / follow-up message (you can send now or save as a draft)
- Set a reminder for a follow-up call or to send photos/links you mentioned
- Save photos or draft a short family-update note

If you want a follow-up message, pick one to send/edit and tell me whether to send now or save as a draft:

1) Short & friendly
- Subject: Great catching up yesterday
- Body: Hi Sarah — it was so nice catching up over virtual coffee yesterday and hearing about the family. Let’s do it again soon! Love, [Your name]

2) Share photos / suggest next call
- Subject: Loved our chat — photos & next time?
- Body: Hi Sarah — I enjoyed our virtual coffee yesterday. I’m attaching a couple of photos I mentioned — would you like to schedule another call next week? — [Your name]

3) Family-focused follow-up
- Subject: So nice to hear about your family
- Body: Hi Sarah — I really enjoyed hearing your updates about the kids and everything going on at home. If you want, I can send that recipe/book link I mentioned — would you like it? Best, [Your name]

Which option (or a custom message) and do you want me to send or save it as a draft?

User: I had a great time trying out a new recipe with my friend Jessica at the cooking class last night.
Assistant: Sounds wonderful — glad you had a fun time! Would you like me to save this as a memory (so I can use it later), or draft/send a follow-up to Jessica? I can also search your inbox for her contact if you don’t have her email handy.

Here are three quick message options — tell me which one to send (or edit), and whether to send now or save as a draft. If you want me to send, either give Jessica’s email or ask me to search for her (suggest a search phrase like “Jessica cooking class” or “Jessica [last name]”).

1) Short thank-you
- Subject: Great meeting you at the cooking class
- Body: Hi Jessica — it was great meeting you at the cooking class last night. I had a lot of fun trying the new recipe with you. Thanks for the company — would you like to swap notes or try another class soon? Best, [Your name]

2) Share recipe/photos + follow-up
- Subject: Recipe & photos from last night
- Body: Hi Jessica — I had a great time at the cooking class last night. I’m attaching the recipe notes and a couple of photos I took. If you’re up for it, would you like to try the recipe together next weekend? Cheers, [Your name]

3) Friendly / keep in touch
- Subject: Loved cooking together last night
- Body: Hi Jessica — I really enjoyed cooking together at class last night and trying that new recipe. It’d be great to get together again — coffee or another class sometime? Best, [Your name]

What would you like me to do: save as a memory, draft one of these, or send it now? If sending, do you want me to search for Jessica’s email (suggest a search phrase) or do you have her address?

User: Please remember that I went on a weekend trip to the mountains with my friend Alex, and we had a great time hiking and exploring the scenic trails.
Assistant: Got it — I’ll remember that you went on a weekend trip to the mountains with your friend Alex and had a great time hiking and exploring the trails.

Would you like to add any details now (trip dates, which trails you hiked, photos, which Alex this is, highlights or a favorite photo)? I can also do any of the following:

- Save the memory as-is (already saved).
- Draft or send a follow-up message to Alex (I can search your inbox for Alex’s contact if you want).
- Save or organize trip photos / create a short trip summary you can share.
- Set a reminder to plan a return trip or book another hike.
- Find related emails (reservations, maps, or gear receipts) in your inbox.

If you want a follow-up message to Alex, here are three quick options — tell me which one to send (or edit), and whether to send now or save as a draft:

1) Short & friendly
- Subject: Great trip!
- Body: Hey Alex — I had a great time hiking this weekend. The trails were beautiful — we should do it again soon!

2) Share photos & highlights
- Subject: Weekend photos & highlights
- Body: Hey Alex — loved the hike this weekend. I’m attaching a few photos I took — my favorite was [spot]. Want to plan another trip next month?

3) Thank-you / plan next
- Subject: Thanks for the weekend — next trip?
- Body: Hi Alex — thanks for the fun trip to the mountains. I enjoyed exploring the trails with you. Want to pick a date for another hike?

Which would you like, or do you just want me to keep this memory?

Assistant: You talked about your upcoming trip to Italy.

Would you like me to do anything with that — for example, add trip details to your memory (dates/places), search your inbox for Emily’s contact and draft a follow-up message, or set reminders for planning tasks?
